hitl_conditions: Planner states the structural change in natural language; agents plan via RAG, retrieve OFacT documentation/state model and execute edits; planner reviews responses and a validation step confirms intent alignment; simulation-expert step instructions eliminated; real-planner evaluation pending.
key_finding: Agentic LLM system (five Smolagents code agents, ReAct, RAG over OFacT documentation/state model; Qwen3-32B) lets non-experts structurally adapt an event-log-generated material-flow twin of a lab assembly factory via natural language; lean multi-agent, RAG planning and non-reasoning LLMs performed best (up to 100% success), removing expert-authored step instructions.

quotes.text: Simulation-based digital twins are a core foundation for the efficient and holistic optimization of material-flow systems across the lifecycle – from design and planning to control. However, constructing digital representations of supply chains and production/logistics systems is labor-intensive and largely manual.

...with in-line quality tests after each station as well as mobile robots for parts supply. It supports automated assembly and disassembly without human intervention. The SBDT was auto-generated from factory event logs using OFacT.

...an LLM-based design assistant, which performs modeling through natural-language interaction with non-expert users. The assistant employs an agentic, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) workflow and relies exclusively on publicly available information from the open-source digital-twin platform OpenFactoryTwin (OFacT) to execute adaptations.

We measured total modification time (end-to-end adaptation duration) and user interaction time (time spent composing prompts and reviewing responses) and success rates. All tests used the Qwen3-32B model.
...where the new framework required more user time, likely due to an additional validation step to ensure alignment with the user's intent (Figure 2).
quotes.section: 4.3 Results from Comparison with Former Framework

quotes.text: To enable supply chain and production planners to directly adapt SBDTs during (re)design, we propose shifting from a single-agent LLM to an agentic AI, thereby increasing flexibility and minimizing DT-specific engineering (e.g., step instructions).

ft_note: Incluido: SBDT de flujo de materiales (OFacT, autogenerado de event logs; IoT-Factory de laboratorio) adaptado por IA agéntica (5 agentes Smolagents, ReAct, RAG, Qwen3-32B) vía lenguaje natural del planificador no experto, que redacta prompts y valida resultados.
